description: Action types and risk events for the agent governance pipeline. Risk events carry incident_reference + framework_source_url for audit defensibility. See SOURCES.md.
grounding_note: Incidents and framework citations are public, defensible references — not claims about prevention. Customers calibrate severity and alerting thresholds locally.

incident_reference.name: ChatGPT — Redis bug exposed conversation titles and payment metadata
incident_reference.summary: Request-cancellation race in redis-py exposed chat titles and partial payment data for ~1.2% of ChatGPT Plus subscribers. Canonical 'shared cache + agent output' PII-leak class.

incident_reference.name: Samsung — semiconductor source code pasted into ChatGPT
incident_reference.summary: Three separate engineer-driven leaks of proprietary semiconductor source code and meeting transcripts to ChatGPT within 20 days. Samsung banned generative-AI tools company-wide on 2023-05-01.

incident_reference.name: Meta — Irish DPC €390M fine for Article 6 violation
incident_reference.summary: Irish Data Protection Commission fined Meta €210M (Facebook) + €180M (Instagram) for relying on 'contract' legal basis to process personal data for behavioural advertising without valid consent. Canonical 'consent assumed not captured' GDPR case.

incident_reference.name: Capital One — SSRF to AWS metadata service
incident_reference.summary: WAF misconfiguration allowed SSRF; attacker reached EC2 instance metadata service and exfiltrated ~106M records to external infrastructure. $80M OCC fine; consent order specifically cited absent egress controls.

incident_reference.name: Samsung — proprietary code to external LLM endpoint
incident_reference.summary: Engineer-initiated paste of proprietary semiconductor code to a third-party model service — the canonical agent-era external-flow violation (the destination is a model API, not a competitor).

incident_reference.name: CVE-2025-49596 — MCP Inspector RCE (CVSS 9.4)
incident_reference.summary: Unauthenticated MCP Inspector instances allowed arbitrary command execution — an agent-tooling 'open scope' failure exposed to network.

incident_reference.name: Tool-mutation / rug-pull pattern (Simon Willison)
incident_reference.summary: MCP tool definitions can mutate after install; a tool approved on Day 1 can be re-pointed by Day 7 with no re-approval. The scope a user authorized is not the scope the tool ends up exercising.

incident_reference.name: Moffatt v. Air Canada — airline liable for chatbot hallucination
incident_reference.summary: BC Civil Resolution Tribunal held Air Canada liable for chatbot-invented bereavement-refund policy ($812.02). Court rejected airline's 'separate legal entity' defence — companies own their agents' decisions. The first agent-confidence ruling that bit a deployer.

incident_reference.name: Zillow Offers — model drift in production
incident_reference.summary: iBuying model overpaid for inventory in a volatile market; Zillow wound down Offers with a $304M write-down and ~25% workforce reduction. Confidence intervals existed; they did not surface to a decision veto in time.

incident_reference.name: Atlassian Cloud — 14-day partial outage
incident_reference.summary: Maintenance script deleted ~775 customer sites; recovery took up to 14 days for some tenants because per-tenant restore tooling and lineage between operational and backup state did not exist.

incident_reference.name: Amazon — CNPD €746M fine (Luxembourg)
incident_reference.summary: Largest GDPR fine to date at issuance; Luxembourg DPA found Amazon's personal-data processing did not comply with GDPR rules, including retention and lawful-basis concerns.

incident_reference.name: MCPTox benchmark — agent vulnerability to tool-output prompt injection
incident_reference.summary: Benchmark tested 20 LLM agents against 45 real MCP servers; most agents were vulnerable to prompt-injection-driven action loops via tool descriptions and outputs. Loops are the failure mode; injection is the trigger.

target_classes._note: r56 consequence-driven severity: effectful_tools are tools whose execution ACTS on the world (funds movement, credit inquiry, outbound customer comms); record_stores are books-and-records-shaped sinks whose write integrity the 17a-4 preservation obligation cares about. The classifier derives severity from these classes + the trace's own fields; severity_default is the class floor, rendered only in the pattern precedent register.
